By this judgment, I will dispose off the present eviction petition (amended) filed by the petitioner Babu Ram Aggarwal against the respondents under section 14 (1) (e) of Delhi Rent Control Act 1958, thereby praying that an order of eviction be passed in his favour and against the respondents in respect of tenanted shop with loft and open verandah i.e. E34/3, Main Market, Hauz Khas, New Delhi, forming part of property bearing No.E34, Main Market, Hauz Khas, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as the "suit shop/premises") on the ground of bonafide requirement of the petitioner. 2. Brief case of the petitioner as per eviction petition (amended) is that he is the owner landlord of property in question and he requires the suit shop for himself because he does not have reasonably suitable commercial accommodation. It is stated that respondents herein are the tenants of petitioner and respondent no.1, 3 & 4 namely Krishan Kumar, Anil Kumar and Rishi Kumar are running a hardware shop in the name of style of Aggarwal Bros & Co. from the premises in question. It is further stated that suit shop was in possession of late Sh. Satnarain Aggarwal till his death and CS No. 6170/16 Babu Ram Aggarwal v. Krishan Kumar Pages 2/18 after his death, the same is in possession of respondents. It is stated that the last monthly rent of Rs.490/ . 3. As per petitioner, the premises was in possession of tenant late Sh. Satnarain Aggarwal at the time of purchase by the petitioner on 30.01.2003. It is averred that petitioner is also owner of two adjoining shops i.e. E34/1 & E34/2 forming part of the property No.E34, Main Market, Hauz Khas, New Delhi but the same are in possession, occupation and use of M/s Bazar Private Ltd and the civil proceedings are pending between petitioner and lessee M/s Star Bazar Pvt Ltd in the court of law. 4. It is further averred that property No.E34 is measuring 212 Sq Yards and the portion shown in green colour was owned by wife of petitioner. It is stated that after filing of eviction petition, Smt. Jayawanti Aggarwal came into possession of the petitioner and his son Pankaj Aggarwal, but the said portion do not meet with requirement of the petitioner and his family members. 5. It is further stated that at present, the family of petitioner consists of his son, daughterinlaw, two grand children and five married daughters. It is stated that petitioner has to help his daughters financially time to time as per their requirement. It is stated that petitioner and his son are the earning members and they have scope of improving their financial status enabling them to meet not only the requirement of his family but also the financial condition of his daughters, for expansion of the business and for financial improvement and therefore the petitioner requires tenanted premises. 6. It is further averred that property consists of ground floor, loft on mezzanine floor and one room with open terrace at the first floor. Mezzanine floor and one room on the first floor is in possession and occupation of the petitioner and his son Pankaj Aggarwal and they are using the same for storage and office purpose. As per petitioner, the ground floor portion except the suit shop, is in possession of the petitioner and the son of the petitioner is running departmental store. It is stated that at the time of filing of petition, the son of petitioner was running the business of Vodafone dealership but due to old age of the petitioner, he required his son as helping hand as well as to expand business for helping the family members financially and as a consequence thereof, son of petitioner left the vodafone dealership in February 2014 and started working with the petitioner. 8. It is stated that back portion measuring 200 Sq Feet of the said shop is owned by Jyoti Aggarwal i.e. daughterin l a w o f t h e p e t i t i o n e r a n d p e t i t i o n e r i s p a y i n g r e n t o f R s . 1 5 0 0 0 / p e r m o n t h to her. Thereafter, the petitioner has leased out two shops No.1 & 2 in property no. E34 to M/s Star Bazar through its Director Mr. Naveen Malhotra for a period of nine years vide registered lease deed registered on 07.02.2012, for an area of approx 770 Sq Feet for running a retail outlet, however the actual area is approx 910 Sq Feet which has been concealed by petitioner with malafide intention. It is stated that even Smt. Jaywanti, wife of petitioner leased out the rear portion of E34 measuring approx 330 Sq Feet of property to M/s Star B a z a r f o r a p e r i o d o f n i n e y e a r s v i d e r e g i s t e r e d l e a s e d e e d registered on 07.02.2012 for running a retail outlet. M/s Star Bazar vacated both the said premises during the pendency of present petition, around 31st October, 2013. 16. It is denied that the portion shown in green color was owned by wife of petitioner. It is further denied that after her demise, the daughters of petitioner alongwith petitioner relinquished their share in the said property in favour of son of the petitioner and he became owner of said portion. It is further denied that the portion shown in green color came into possession of the petitioner and his son but the same do not meet with the requirement of the petitioner and his family members.

Thereafter, replication was filed by the petitioner to the amended WS of respondents denying all the allegation/averments of the respondent. It is stated that site plan is correct and correctly depict the tenanted premises as well as remaining portions as on date of filing of petition. 23. It is denied that petitioner has made baseless and bogus allegations against the respondent. The petitioner has raised his bonafide requirement on two grounds. Firstly, he requires additional finances to maintain his family which include his six daughters who are still financially dependent on him as he renders them financial assistance time to time. The second and the main ground raised by petitioner regarding his bonafide requirement is that he is doing the business of distribution of pharmaceuticals from the mezzanine floor which is insufficient and unsuitable for the expansion of said Sh. It is claimed that the petitioner requires the demised premises for starting his retail business of pharmaceutical/medicines. It is submitted that the area is adjoining to two big hospitals i.e. AIIMS and Safdarjung and the ground floor premises is better suited for the same and is on the main road also. 34. The contours of bonafide requirement have been discussed in detail by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the judgment of Shiv Sarup Gupta v. Dr. Mahesh Chand Gupta (1999) 6 SCC 222. It has been observed therein "thus the term bonafide or genuinely refers to a state of mind. Requirement is not a mere desire. The degree of intensity contemplated by 'requires' is much more higher than in mere desire. The phrase 'required bona fide' is suggestive of legislative intent that a mere desire which is outcome of whim or fancy is not taken note of by the Rent Control Legislation. However, he also deposed that all of them are income tax assessee. Thus, it is hard to believe that the daughters of petitioner are financially dependent on him as not only they are married and living separately from petitioner, but their husbands are also doing jobs/businesses and are income tax payees. Further, he has deposed that he has given financial help to his daughters as and when required. This shows that admittedly daughters of petitioner are not financially dependent on him for their day to day life. Moreover, he failed to tell as to when he had rendered financial help to them. C S N o . 6 1 7 0 / 1 6 B a b u R a m A g g a r w a l v . The petitioner has also claimed that her family includes his son, daughter in law and two grand children and that he wants to expand his business for financial improvement of his family. Thus, he has presented a picture of jointness of his family. However, at the same time, he has pleaded that he is paying rent of Rs. 15,000/ to his daughter in law for the back portion of the property. Thus, both of these facts are irreconcilable. Moreover, as discussed later, it is revealed that the son of petitioner is working as an employee of petitioner in the departmental store which is being run by proprietorship of petitioner. Such kind of set up is also against the joint family system of Hindu Undivided Family. A c c o r d i n g l y , t h e p l e a o f p e t i t i o n e r t h a t h e w a n t s p r e m i s e s f o r financial improvement of his family is on a very weak footing. In regard to the requirement of the petitioner to shift his business from the mezzanine floor to the suit shop, the Counsel for respondent has submitted that there are number of facts which show that shop in question is not required by the petitioner for any such bonafide need. It is submitted that petitioner voluntarily shifted to mezzanine floor despite earlier doing his business from the ground floor premises only. It is submitted that petitioner is running a distributorship business which does not require footfall of the public. It is argued that even otherwise the petitioner and his family members had let out the other shops available at the ground floor in the recent times and the same negates any bonafide requirement of the petitioner of any ground floor property i.e. the suit shop. It is submitted that even when the petitioner got a large area at the ground floor still he did not start any pharmaceutical retail business Sh. Babu Ram Aggarwal vs Sh. Krishan Kumar on 12 November, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187121960/ 11 from there. Same shows that petitioner has no bonafide requirement for the alleged business venture. On the other hand, Counsel for petitioner has argued that initially CS No. 6 1 7 0 / 1 6 B a b u R a m A g g a r w a l v . K r i s h a n K u m a r P a g e s 1 4 / 1 8 the petitioner shifted his business to the mezzanine floor as he was facing financial difficulty and had to let out the shops of ground floor to other tenants. It is further submitted after eviction of the tenants from the other shops the said portion is being used by the son of petitioner and, therefore, the requirement of petitioner qua the suit shop is still persisting. I have considered the submissions of both parties.

Jai Bhagwan Gupta and his wife and Sh. Prabodh Chaudhary vide two registered agreements dated 03.01.2012, which shows that the petitioner is indulged in selling residentialcumcommercial properties. The allegations of non payment of rent is totally baseless and malafide. It is stated that petitioner has been intentionally not accepting rent tendered to him. Lastly, it is stated that petitioner has no case for grant of eviction as the petition has no merits and it deserves to be dismissed. 22. Thereafter, replication was filed by the petitioner to the amended WS of respondents denying all the allegation/averments of the respondent. It is stated that WS is defective and not in accordance with law. It is stated that site plan is correct and correctly depict the tenanted premises as well as remaining portions as on date of filing of petition. 23. It is denied that petitioner has made baseless and bogus allegations against the respondent. In regard to the requirement of the petitioner to shift his business from the mezzanine floor to the suit shop, the Counsel for respondent has submitted that there are number of facts which show that shop in question is not required by the petitioner for any such bonafide need. It is submitted that petitioner voluntarily shifted to mezzanine floor despite earlier doing his business from the ground floor premises only. It is submitted that petitioner is running a distributorship business which does not require footfall of the public. It is argued that even otherwise the petitioner and his family members had let out the other shops available at the ground floor in the recent times and the same negates any bonafide requirement of the petitioner of any ground floor property i.e. the suit shop. It is submitted that even when the petitioner got a large area at the ground floor still he did not start any pharmaceutical retail business Sh. Babu Ram Aggarwal vs Sh. Krishan Kumar on 12 November, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187121960/ 11 from there. Same shows that petitioner has no bonafide requirement for the alleged business venture. On the other hand, Counsel for petitioner has argued that initially CS No. 6 1 7 0 / 1 6 B a b u R a m A g g a r w a l v . K r i s h a n K u m a r P a g e s 1 4 / 1 8 the petitioner shifted his business to the mezzanine floor as he was facing financial difficulty and had to let out the shops of ground floor to other tenants. It is further submitted after eviction of the tenants from the other shops the said portion is being used by the son of petitioner and, therefore, the requirement of petitioner qua the suit shop is still persisting. I have considered the submissions of both parties.
